stemMd: Which pair of neutral atoms in their ground states is expected to have similar chemical behaviour because each has one electron in its outermost occupied shell?
explanationMd: Atomic number gives the electron count of a neutral atom. The shell arrangements for atomic numbers 3 and 11 are 2,1 and 2,8,1. Each has one outer-shell electron and can form a +1 ion by losing it. The other listed pairs do not both have one outer-shell electron.

distractorRationale.e: The outer-shell counts are four and five, rather than one in each atom.
distractorRationale.a: The outer-shell counts are six and eight.
distractorRationale.d: The outer-shell counts are one and two, so only the first meets the stated criterion.
distractorRationale.b: The outer-shell counts are eight and one, not one in both.
